text.p: Israeli bonds closed virtually unchanged on Wednesday in quiet trading and traders said the market had stabilised at the current level.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.04 pct to 101.70
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.02 pct to 101.05.
Volume was moderate at 152 million shekels.

"Mutual funds continue to invest in bonds but investors are focusing on the stock market. The market was very quiet and the is expected to remain stable," said Gidi Halperin, investment manger at Meitav Securiteis and Investments.
"Unlinked bonds were rising on hopes for declining inflation in 1997. Yields have fallen sharply, but some investors believe that unlinked bonds are still attractive," Halperin added.
Makams closed slightly higher. Traders said that dollar-linked bonds posted the highest rise as the U.S. currency soared to its highest levels in years on overseas markets.
In the local foreign currency market the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2970 shekels against 3.2840 shekels on Tuesday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
